subject: Handback & verification: customer-controlled storage and remote-sweep proof
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sentinel Health Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handback proof & remote sweep procedures

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal pulled together a short list of questions we need answered before finalizing the Private/VPC SOW. Broadly: how does Redwood enable customer-controlled storage and what form of evidence will you provide that data was actually removed when we terminate? Specific asks below — please keep answers practical and prescriptive so we can include language in the SOW.

1) Can Sentinel keep its own encryption keys (KMS/HSM) in a Private VPC deployment? If so, what exact operations does Redwood perform on encrypted objects during a wipe?
2) We require irrefutable proof of deletion for regulated data: are you able to produce a signed, time-stamped attestation (packaged PDF) showing the sequence of delete operations, snapshots purged, and key zeroization? Who signs it?
3) Do you retain any residual snapshots or backups after a tenant handback? If yes, how are they purged and what is the timeline?
4) For an audit, we may request a notarized third-party confirmation (notary or forensic firm). Are you able to coordinate a third-party witness or provide a chain of custody that a third party can verify?

I've attached our compliance checklist (Sentinel-Compliance-Reqs.pdf) with redlines. Can we get a technical runbook and an estimate of how long it would take to produce the evidence package post-termination?

Appreciate a prompt reply — we need to close the language this week.

Best,
Amanda Li
Head of IT Security
Sentinel Health

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Handback proof & remote sweep procedures

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: yes, Private deployments can use customer-managed keys; Redwood supports both customer-hosted KMS and integration with cloud KMS/HSM. We offer two certified handback modes (customer-led and assisted) and produce an evidentiary package that includes signed deletion manifests, an append-only audit trail, and optional notarized witness. High-level answers below, followed by a short ops runbook and next steps.

High-level commitments:
- Customer-managed keys: supported. You control key lifecycle; Redwood performs crypto-erase operations against objects only after receiving a signed deletion request and after keys are zeroized per your policy.
- Evidence package: we generate a time-stamped, signed attestation (PDF) containing: list of deleted objects, snapshot IDs removed, KMS key disposition (zeroize/rotation logs), operator runbook steps executed, and SHA256 rollup hashes of deleted object manifests. The attestation is signed by Redwood Privacy Ops (Naomi Feldman) and includes an HMAC of the manifest for tamper-evidence.
- Snapshots/backups: persistent snapshots are purged as part of the handback workflow. We do not retain long-term backups for customer-owned volumes beyond configured retention; default purge is performed within 48 hours of handback, with a 0-7 day configurable observation window (for safety rollback) — this window is documented in the SOW.
- Third-party witness: we can coordinate a mutually agreed third-party (forensic or notary) to observe the procedure and countersign the attestation. Alternatively, we can provide cryptographic proof (signed hashes published to an append-only ledger) that a third party can verify independently.

Technical runbook (condensed):
1) Pre-handback: confirm final snapshot policy and KMS mode (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed). Capture pre-handback snapshot of object manifests and compute SHA256 digests.
2) Key zeroization: if customer-managed keys are provided for zeroization, Redwood triggers KMS zeroize API under customer authorization. If keys are customer-held, Redwood requires signed authorization to proceed.
3) Data purge: delete object records, irrecoverably remove local KV cache, and issue snapshot purge commands to storage layer.
4) Audit capture: stream deletion events to append-only audit store; compute rollup hash and sign with Redwood Privacy Ops key.
5) Evidence package: compile manifest, event logs, signed rollup, and operator checklist into a PDF attestation. Optionally arrange third-party witness.

Estimated timeline: 7 business days from signed termination/authorization to a completed evidence package in a standard scenario. If notarization and on-site witness are requested, plan for 10-15 business days.

I've attached a short options doc (Redwood-Handback-Options.pdf) and a Wipe-Proof spec spreadsheet that maps each step to evidence artifacts.

Action items:
- Amanda: confirm KMS preference (customer-managed preferred per your note?) and whether you want third-party witness.
- Marissa: please schedule a 60-minute technical walkthrough with Sentinel next day.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Amanda Li <amanda@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sentinel Health Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Handback & verification: customer-controlled storage and remote-sweep proof

Thanks Karthik — that helps. A few clarifications from Legal and Compliance:

- Timeline: our auditors require the evidence package to be deliverable within 30 calendar days of contract termination. Your 7 business day estimate is acceptable if guaranteed in the SOW; please confirm you can commit to that SLA.
- Signed attestation: Legal prefers the attestation to be signed by an officer-level privacy or security exec and include a statement of no residual copies in any Redwood-managed backups. Who would sign on Redwood's side?
- Tamper evidence: rather than an HMAC only, we'd prefer a signed SHA256 rollup published to a public timestamping service (or ledger) so an independent auditor can verify that the evidence hasn't been altered. Can you support publishing the hash?
- Third-party witness: we'd like to reserve the right for a third-party forensic firm to perform a verification. Please confirm Redwood will: (a) permit an agreed-upon third party to observe the purge workflow remotely or on-site (depending on deployment), and (b) provide chain of custody logs for the witnessing period.

We'd also like to see the runbook in more detail so our security team can vet it. Can Marissa share a runbook PDF and a proposed SOW clause we can circulate to Legal?

Amanda

--
Attachment: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sentinel Health Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Handback & verification: customer-controlled storage and remote-sweep proof

Amanda — hi, Naomi from Privacy Ops here. I'll take ownership of the attestation and the runbook details. Short answers to your points and a confirmation of Redwood commitments below.

1) SLA for evidence package: Redwood can commit to a 7-business-day deliverable for the standard evidence package following receipt of signed termination authorization and access to required KMS operations. We'll add this as an SLA line in the SOW (7 business days, escalatable to 3 business days for an express fee).

2) Signatory: attestation will be signed by me (Head of Privacy Ops) and countersigned by the VP of Security if Legal requires officer-level signature. The attestation explicitly states that no residual copies exist in Redwood-managed backups at the time of submission.

3) Tamper-proofing: we support publishing the SHA256 rollup to a public timestamping service (RFC 3161) or to an append-only ledger (we've used a neutral timestamping provider before). We'll include the timestamp receipt in the final package so auditors can verify immutability.

4) Third-party witness and chain of custody: we will coordinate with your selected third-party forensic firm. For Private/VPC customers we can:
- Enable remote observation via secure session (recommended for most cases) and provide live deletion logs; or
- Support on-site witness for air-gapped/on-prem deployments subject to standard security onboarding.
We will produce a chain of custody report for the witness window, including operator identities, command timestamps, and storage node identifiers.

5) Detailed runbook: Marissa will share the full runbook PDF and a redlined SOW clause that covers the SLA, evidence contents, and optional notarization.

Next steps:
- Marissa: attach runbook + SOW clause and propose 3 time slots for the walkthrough.
- Amanda: confirm KMS mode (customer-managed confirmed?) and whether Sentinel wants public timestamping or ledger publication.
- Once confirmed, we'll include the 7-business-day SLA and notarization options in the SOW amendment and provide pricing for notarized/onsite witness.

Thanks — I'll be the point for the attestation and will sign the final package.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Ops | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
